targets.approach: Take the Beehive Lake trail from the Pack River side up to the lake. Curve around the southeast (left) shore of the lake, swing left round the little peak, and descend into the Slide Creek drainage, which offers camping and water. The route lies on a wall facing north along South Twin Peak's eastern ridge, southwest of Beehive Lake, at the head of that drainage.
targets.descent_text: Rappel the route from its stainless-steel rappel stations, with a little downscrambling along the way.
targets.name: The Dodgy Selkirk Boys

targets.approach: Take the Beehive Lake trail from the Pack River side up to the lake. Pass the lake on its right and go up through talus and heathery meadows to the notch on the left flank of North Twin Peak, the right-hand summit as you reach the water. Drop a few feet over the saddle and traverse right until you are below the route. A short scramble reaches a narrow ledge with a gnarled whitebark pine, which is the belay for the first pitch. The corner is on the southeast edge of North Twin Peak.
targets.name: The Xanthic Corner

targets.approach: From Priest Lake, drive the Hunt Creek road to the Horton Ridge trailhead and follow the Horton Ridge trail toward Chimney Rock and Mount Roothaan. The east face of Roothaan's northeast ridge is reached from the west by dropping into the west-face basin of Chimney Rock and traversing below its north face, or, more efficiently, by traversing across Roothaan and descending the corridor between its summit pyramid and the north-ridge cirque wall. The route is next to Chimney Rock, on a natural line splitting the upper face above a juniper-covered ledge, which has a bolted rappel station on its left.
targets.descent_text: Rappel the route, or walk off.
targets.name: Kaniksu Jiu Jitsu

targets.approach: From Priest Lake, drive the Hunt Creek road to the Horton Ridge trailhead and follow the Horton Ridge trail toward Chimney Rock and Mount Roothaan. Chimney Rock is a three-sided granite tower. Reach the west-face basin and wrap around the tower's south end, then scramble onto a wide ledge that leads round onto the east face. The start is a big detached flake for laybacking, which gives access to a seam through a smooth stretch of wall.
targets.name: Tarzan

targets.approach: Take the boat across Redfish Lake (or hike around it) and go up the main drainage toward the Grand Mogul; the Perch lies up the second side drainage on the left beyond it. Watch for the point where the main trail comes nearest the creek, a little beyond the third footbridge; leave the trail there, cross the creek on logs, and the smaller trail then leads up and to the right into the basin beneath the Perch. Fish Ladder is a short crack directly below a flat campsite above the lake, next to a popular rock jump.
targets.name: Fish Ladder

targets.approach: Take the boat across Redfish Lake (or hike around it) and go up the main drainage toward the Grand Mogul; the Perch lies up the second side drainage on the left beyond it. Watch for the point where the main trail comes nearest the creek, a little beyond the third footbridge; leave the trail there, cross the creek on logs, and the smaller trail then leads up and to the right into the basin beneath the Perch. Fish Scales is a splitter crack with a small tree growing in it, a short distance left of Fish Ladder.
targets.name: Fish Scales

targets.approach: Take the boat across Redfish Lake (or hike around it) and go up the main drainage toward the Grand Mogul; the Perch lies up the second side drainage on the left beyond it. Watch for the point where the main trail comes nearest the creek, a little beyond the third footbridge; leave the trail there, cross the creek on logs, and the smaller trail then leads up and to the right into the basin beneath the Perch. Fountain of Youth replaces the opening pitch of Boomer's Story with a more direct line, taking the clear seam beneath it, which becomes a left-facing dihedral partway up.
targets.name: Fountain of Youth

targets.approach: Take the boat across Redfish Lake (or hike around it) and go up the main drainage toward the Grand Mogul; the Perch lies up the second side drainage on the left beyond it. Watch for the point where the main trail comes nearest the creek, a little beyond the third footbridge; leave the trail there, cross the creek on logs, and the smaller trail then leads up and to the right into the basin beneath the Perch. Pandemonium Palace is on the far left side of the Perch. Either go up as for the main routes and then continue left with some fifth-class scrambling, or leave the approach trail early near the talus field and cut up and left. In either case aim for a big right-facing dihedral, which serves as an approach pitch to the large ledge with a huge whitebark pine where the route officially begins.
targets.name: Pandemonium Palace

targets.approach: Take the boat across Redfish Lake (or hike around it) and go up the main drainage toward the Grand Mogul; the Perch lies up the second side drainage on the left beyond it. Watch for the point where the main trail comes nearest the creek, a little beyond the third footbridge; leave the trail there, cross the creek on logs, and the smaller trail then leads up and to the right into the basin beneath the Perch. The start is a large, plainly visible right-facing flake, left of where Beckey Direct begins.
targets.descent_text: Rappel from the tree above, using slings.
targets.name: Slipstream (first pitch)

targets.approach: Hakuna Matata begins at the centre of the north face, far below the big left-facing corner that dominates it. Shadowlands is in the shallow dihedral system a short distance left, and Lion Tamer begins somewhat further right. The route finishes where it joins Lion Tamer partway up the face.
targets.name: Hakuna Matata

targets.approach: Shadowlands begins at the centre of the north face, in a shallow dihedral immediately right of the conspicuous left-facing corner, and ends on top of Pride Rock, the tower in the centre of the upper face.
targets.descent_text: Rappel the route, or continue to the top via Lion Tamer.
targets.name: Shadowlands

targets.approach: Just south of Challis on Highway 75, leave the car at the pullout by the north end of the bridge; the pillar is easy to see looking west up the dry wash. Hike up the wash, take the left fork at the branch, and climb the loose talus to the gully east of the pillar. From the gully at the base, go up it and scramble over ledges on the left side to an obvious notch where a single-bolt belay with a quick link starts the climb.
targets.descent_text: Rappel from the single-bolt anchor on top, then continue down from the notch anchor.
targets.name: Pillar pandemicas

targets.approach: Descend to where the trail fords the creek west of the saddle, and follow it beyond the ford to another small stream, then go up a steep, sandy rise. From the top of the hill the large formations on the left are the King Pin and Queen Pin, facing each other across a corridor of pine trees, with the King Pin to the north and the Queen Pin to the south. Princess Died is on the Queen Pin directly across the pine corridor from Kind Tut on the King Pin; it starts on a small ledge.
targets.name: Princess Died

targets.approach: The South Slab is the easiest way up the peak, occupying the left-hand side of the south face.
targets.descent_text: The slab is also the standard way down the peak.
targets.name: South Slab

targets.approach: From the parking lot walk west through the woods on the cut trail, following cairns and boulder-hopping through dead trees to the top of the boulder field on the climber's left. A cairn marks the traverse across the hillside that puts you below a prominent flake with a runoff creek on your left. Descend beside the runoff through the shrubs and along the foot of the slab, cross a log, then continue northwest across the apron toward the big pines, following cairns. Go up past the pines, then down to a sappy pine and traverse a short slab section carefully to a ledge stepping down, keeping to the inside past a big dead tree; this opens onto the slab. Stay on the goat trail.
targets.name: Strawberry Falls

targets.approach: Start as for the Elephant's Perch: take the boat across Redfish Lake or hike around it, then follow the main trail until it crosses several wooden boardwalks. Just beyond them a faint social trail climbs to the slabs. Bacon and Legs begins with a water groove just left of the Central Gully.
targets.name: Bacon and Legs

targets.approach: From Grandjean, a long hike up the trail reaches the bottom lake of the Trail Creek Lakes. The route is the giant dihedral across from where the trail meets the lake.
targets.descent_text: Rappel off the tree at the nose of the cliff, which carries webbing and a ring.
targets.name: Before the rain…

targets.approach: Fugitive is on the west face, just left of Catacombs. It climbs an easy slab below a corner and then a crack system into a tight dihedral.
targets.descent_text: A tree about twenty feet back from the top-out serves as an anchor, and the route can be rappelled with two ropes.
targets.name: Fugitive

targets.approach: From Priest Lake, drive the Hunt Creek road to the Horton Ridge trailhead and follow the Horton Ridge trail toward Chimney Rock and Mount Roothaan. The west face of Roothaan's northeast ridge is the wall you see when approaching from the Priest Lake side; reach its basin from the Horton Ridge trail. North Nose climbs the west side of the north nose of the cirque wall, undercling-traversing a roof near the top to reach a notch.
targets.name: North Nose

targets.approach: From Priest Lake, drive the Hunt Creek road to the Horton Ridge trailhead and follow the Horton Ridge trail toward Chimney Rock and Mount Roothaan. The west face of Roothaan's northeast ridge is the wall you see when approaching from the Priest Lake side. The chimney splits the west face of the north-ridge cirque wall and is passed directly underneath on the short scramble toward Chimney Rock's west face. The lower part is a dirt-floored gully before the chimney proper begins.
targets.name: The Great Chimney
